g.text: Cross-section across a plate margin (not to scale)
The arrows point towards each other: the plates converge.
At the trench the oceanic slab bends down and descends beneath
the overriding continental plate into the mantle.
The volcanoes lie on the overriding plate, inland from the
Why there: water released from the descending slab lowers the
melting temperature of the mantle above it, and some of that magma
rises to the volcanoes. The slab does not simply melt by friction.
earthquake focus (plate interface and descending slab)
